data.title: Lessons from creating my first text adventure
data.author: kqr
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了文字冒险游戏的制作难度以及作者的亲身经验。作者参加了ParserComp 2025比赛，提交了自己的文字冒险游戏《Lockout》。他指出，尽管与其他类型的游戏相比，文字冒险游戏制作相对简单，但实际仍然具有挑战性。作者前两次尝试因过于 ambitious 而失败，最终通过缩小游戏规模和专注细节完成了《Lockout》。文章还探讨了游戏的范围和细节平衡问题，分为广而简和窄而精两类。现代玩家更偏好细节丰富的游戏，而过于简略的游戏可能会让玩家感到沮丧。作者以《The Plot of the Phantom》为例，展示了广而简风格的游戏体验。总体而言，制作文字冒险游戏需要在广度和细节之间找到合适的平衡。

44464536.article_content:
When I write about
the greatness of text adventures
, I pretend they are easy to
make. They are, compared to many other types of games, but it’s still a bit of a
lie. They’re hard to make.
I made one and submitted it to ParserComp 2025, and here’s what I learned.
My first text adventure: Lockout
Since ParserComp voting has opened, the game is now public, and
you can play it
in your browser
. The game itself reveals what it is about as you progress, so I
won’t write too much about it here. You should be able to finish it in 30–60
minutes. Don’t feel bad about needing hints, especially if you’re new to text
adventures.
Lockout
is my third attempt at making a text adventure. The first two failed
because of ambition.
Scope and richness of world modeling
It’s very easy to accidentally try to create too large a text adventure. My
first attempt was way too ambitious, and would have taken months to finish. I
still love the idea for that, but it had to go. I picked another idea that was
much smaller in scope, but it, too, grew too ambitious. I restarted one more
time, from an idea that was even more pared down, and I was actually able to
finish that game. With the minimalistic scope it took maybe fifteen hours of
active work to create most of the game, and then almost as much time again to
fix the 57 problems I received feedback on from beta testers.
1
1
This is a
large time investment for me, which makes it unlikely I’ll create another one
any time soon, even if I’d really like to.
Scope in text adventures is complicated, because there are two dimensions along
which scope can vary: breadth and detail.
A broad game might have many locations, items, and events, but each is
relatively sparsely implemented. Actions get generic responses, and items are
mainly generic scenery without interesting interactions. This is the style of
some of the earliest text adventures; they had to do it that way due to
technical limitations of the time.
A detailed game might have few locations, items, and events, but those that do
exist are modeled in high detail and interact realistically with each other.
Modern development tools afford insane levels of detail, and it’s up to the
author to set a reasonable limit to the detail included.
Lockout
is in the narrow-but-detailed category. Making a broad
and
detailed game takes a huge effort, so for the hobbyist it boils down to finding
the right tradeoff between breadth and detail.
For better or worse, the community encourages detailed games, and among modern
games, a text adventure that is broad and not detailed stands out as lacking in
implementation. A useful comparison to study this difference is
The Plot of the
Phantom
: a newly released game which was designed in the 1980’s, but
implemented using modern tools. It contrasts with
Lockout
in that it is mainly
in the broad-and-sparse camp, as the following interactions illustrate.
CAVE ENTRANCE
You stand at the base of a sandstone cliff, at the mouth of a large cave. Behind
you to the south, a misty Appalachian forest stretches in all directions. A
weathered sign made of pressure-treated lumber and painted in the style of
National Park signage stands to the right of the cave entrance.
The cave entrance is to the north.
Oh, wow, what sort of cave is this?
> look at cave
You can’t see any such thing.
Huh. Well, what can I find in the direction I came from?
> go south
You can’t go that way.
Why not? I suppose what remains is to enter the cave.
> enter cave
You can’t see any such thing.
Oh right, the cave doesn’t exist in the world, only in the description. Maybe I
have to go inside.
> go in
You can’t go that way.
I could have sworn … I guess I’ll go north to enter.
> go north
LARGE CAVERN
You step into a large open space, a cavern created by seeping
groundwater dissolving the sandstone over many decades. The sandy floor is
strewn with rocks and the damp ceiling hangs low, just a foot or two above your
head.
You’re not the first to find this place. Crumpled beer cans and cigarette butts
are everywhere, and the cold, blackend remains of a firepit sit in the cavern
center, and the eastern wall is blanketed with a remarkable amount of
multicolored graffiti.
To the north, a passage disapppears into the rock, while to the west you can see
a hole just barely wide enough to crawl through.
I’m worried about the safety of the ceiling. Can I get more information?
> look
at ceiling
You can’t see any such thing.
That’s odd. Let’s take some stuff we found here before we move on.
> get beer cans and cigarettes
That’s hardly portable.
This goes on for the rest of
The Plot of the Phantom
. There are a lot of things that appear to
exist, but when the player tries to examine them, they aren’t really there, or
they behave in unexpected ways.
Don’t get me wrong! I finished
The Plot of the Phantom
and I had a lot of fun

data.title: Show HN: Modernized file manager and program manager from Windows 3.x
data.author: electroly
data.article_summary: Heirloom apps项目提供了现代化的Windows经典应用程序，包括Heirloom File Manager和Heirloom Program Manager。File Manager是Windows File Manager的衍生版本，支持高DPI屏幕、回收站、书签、拖放操作以及创建和提取zip压缩文件。Program Manager则是经典Program Manager的重制版，用作启动快捷方式的Start菜单替代品。这些应用程序免费且开源，File Manager基于Microsoft Corporation的许可，而Program Manager则基于Brian Luft的许可。项目包含7个版本，最新版为2025年7月发布的12.1.0，主要使用C++编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Windows 3.x文件管理器和程序管理器的现代化改造的评价和相关技术细节的讨论

不同观点：
• JdeBP认为，某些代码提交（如heirloom项目的提交）显示了原始源代码的特征，特别是针对类型转换和未完全现代化的问题。他还指出，其中"Unicode only"的实现使用了WTF-16，而不是UTF-8，尤其是在Win32环境下使用代码页65001时。

• timbit42批评Windows 3.x的程序管理器和文件管理器，认为它们是系统中最糟糕的部分。他推荐使用IBM的Workplace Shell来替代，并提供了相关开源项目和安装程序的链接。

• neckro23指出，在现代化改造过程中，界面风格存在不一致的问题，例如Vista风格的图标与整体风格不匹配，以及窗口最大化时风格变化的问题。他还提到无法最小化窗口，并建议调整Windows 10的平滑滚动设置以符合“快速、轻量”的审美。

• hulitu对展示的现代化改造持讽刺态度，特别提到1像素的窗口边框和“现代的”滚动条，暗示这些改变可能并不符合真正的现代化标准。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了技术实现的细节，如Unicode处理和代码页的使用，显示出参与者对技术准确性的关注。
• 也有对用户界面和用户体验的批评和建议，反映出用户对视觉一致性和操作流畅性的重视。
• 提供了替代解决方案（如IBM的Workplace Shell），显示出社区对开源和定制化方案的兴趣。

争议焦点：
• 现代化改造的具体实现是否真正达到了“现代化”的标准，特别是在界面一致性和功能性方面。

data.title: Solving Wordle with uv's dependency resolver
data.author: mildbyte
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种利用Python的依赖解析工具`uv`来解决Wordle（单词猜谜游戏）的创新方法。作者之前曾用Poetry的依赖解析器解决过数独问题，而现在利用`uv`工具尝试解决Wordle。文章详细分析了Wordle的规则和反馈机制，将其转化为Python包的依赖关系问题。通过将每个可能的单词表示为一个包，每个字母位置表示为具有多个版本的包，并根据Wordle的反馈（绿色、黄色）设置依赖约束，作者设计了一个能够自动猜测正确单词的系统。文章还提供了具体的实现步骤和代码示例，最终可以在GitHub上获取该解决工具并运行。这种方法展示了利用软件工具解决非传统编程问题的创造性思路。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Soduku（数独）实现、Wordle类似项目的可行性、技术工具使用中的问题和趣闻以及对软件包管理的讨论。

不同观点：
• simonw分享了一个简单的Python数独实现，并提供了一个2008年的类似数独解决方案的链接。他认为数独问题比Wordle更容易理解和实现。
• wordglyph对此回应，询问是否可以为WordGlyph.xyz实现类似的功能，暗示对类似技术实现的兴趣。
• remedan偏离主题，提到使用Firefox扩展Foxy Gestures时遇到的奇怪现象，质疑这是否是JS/CSS的技巧或扩展的bug。

补充讨论：
• kibwen提到可以使用`uv`的包解析器进行更严肃的用途，并提供了一个使用pubgrub-rs库的链接，扩展了关于包管理的讨论。
• davejagoda回应kibwen，提到通过使用完整字母表常量来避免错误，并分享了一次因遗漏字母'u'而导致的冗长错误信息，强调了代码可检查性的重要性。
• Joker_vD对没有将大量"wordle-*"包发布到PyPI表示感谢，表达了对避免包泛滥的赞同。
• stared开玩笑地建议下一步可以用`uv`的依赖解析器来玩Doom，引用了一个先前的讨论，增加了对话的幽默感。
• spelunker半开玩笑地要求将这种技术应用到npm上，暗示npm包管理的复杂性，延续了技术趣闻的讨论。

争议焦点：
• 对话中并没有明显的争议，但remedan的问题偏离了主题，引起了对Firefox扩展问题的短暂讨论，与其他技术实现的讨论稍有脱节。

总体来看，评论主要围绕技术实现的可行性、技术工具使用中的趣闻以及对软件包管理的讨论展开。

Solving Wordle with uv's dependency resolver
7th Jul 2025
•
12 min read
•
Tags:
programming
,
tech
,
why
,
disgusting hacks
Table of Contents
Introduction
Background: Sudoku and Python dependency resolution
What is Wordle
Analysis
Basic building blocks
Greens and yellows
Python dependency rules?
Possible position packages
Feedback packages
Putting this all together: the cursed neural network
Implementation
Package examples
--find-links and wheels
Harness
Bonus round: more efficient guessing
Blooper reel
GitHub
Introduction
In a previous life, I wrote a
Sudoku solver that relied on Poetry's dependency resolver
. We ended up selling that startup to EDB (not because of the Poetry hack), which means that they now own this IP. And, since then, Python packaging has advanced, with
uv
taking the world by storm.
This means that it's time for a refresh. Can we use
uv
instead of Poetry? And can we solve a Wordle instead of a Sudoku?
For the impatient: you can get the solver from
my GitHub
. Run
uv run main.py run
and watch it go.
Background: Sudoku and Python dependency resolution
The short summary of the Sudoku + Poetry post is that unlike Rust or JavaScript, a single Python project cannot use more than one version of a specific Python package. This means that we can easily represent a Sudoku grid as 81 Python packages, each with 9 possible versions. If a certain cell has a specific number (version), cells in the same row, column and a 3x3 square it belongs to cannot have that same number.
We can encode these rules as version constraints on other packages representing our cell's neighbours.
Once we have our 81 packages, all that remains is encoding our problem by making another package, specifying the precise versions of the cells where we already have numbers, leaving the rest as wildcards, and then letting Poetry generate a lockfile that will assign each number (version) to every cell (package), thus solving the puzzle.
What is Wordle
This
is Wordle.
You have six attempts to guess a five-letter word. On each guess, you get what I'll be calling "feedback": each letter in your guess becomes green (correct letter in the correct position), yellow (correct letter, wrong position) or nothing (wrong letter).
In this post, I'll represent it as a string
YGG..
, meaning that the feedback we got for our answer is:
Yellow at position 1
Green at positions 2 and 3
Blank or "dot" at positions 4 and 5
Analysis
It is said that if you ask an LLM to think really hard about its answer and write down its thinking before giving the final response, then it can successfully count the number of r's in the word
strawberrry
and help you sell more inference tokens.
Let's do exactly that and break this down.
Basic building blocks
Let's start simple. The solution to a Wordle is a five-letter word, and we'd like our system to choose one possible word given all information that we feed into it. We can encode this as a single Python package with multiple possible versions, where each version represents a single word. This is a useful building block.
The other building block is that each position can only have one letter in it. We can easily represent this as five "position" packages, each of which can have 26 versions. If the position package 1 has version 2, that means "B" is in that position.
We can then draw dependencies between a specific version of our "word" package to specific versions of our "position" packages. If our word is
STALL
, then it'll depend on:
position package 1, version 19 (S)
position package 2, version 20 (T)
position package 3, version 1 (A)
position packages 4 and 5, version 12 (L)
Greens and yellows
However, this is not enough. We need to encode some more complex facts about the solution in Wordle than we did with Sudoku. For example, let's assume that we guessed
CHILD
and the feedback we got is
..YG.
. This means:
The fourth letter is L
The third letter is not I
But there is at least one I somewhere in the word
None of the letters are C, H or D
Is this correct though? There is a bit of nuance here.
Let's try again, this time with a different guess but the same word. We try
ATOLL
(it's not an optimal play, but as a demonstration) and get
...GY
. Here, we can't just say that there is an L somewhere in the word (because there already is). We have to say that there is at least one L in the first, second or third position.
Now let's say we guess
LILLE
and get
.GGG.
. What does this mean? Just because L in the first position gave us a dot doesn't mean there are no Ls in the word at all (there clearly are). Instead, we need to say that the first and the fifth position don't contain an L.
One thing that stems from this is that the feedback we get for a specific letter in a specific position will change based on other letters in our guess. For example, let's say the real world is
BUNNY
. If we guess
NNNON
, we'll get
YYG.Y
. And if we then guess
NNNNN
, we'll get
..GG.

data.article_summary: 本文讨论了艺术作品中色彩持久性的重要性，即“耐光性”，以及如何选择耐光材料以防止褪色。作者Sarah Renae Clark在过去六个月中对50多个彩铅品牌进行了耐光性测试，将色卡暴露在阳光下并记录变化。文中解释了什么是耐光性、其重要性、测量方法（如蓝羊毛尺度、ASTM D6901标准等），以及作者的测试结果和见解。耐光性对想要作品长久保存的艺术家尤其重要，无论是展示、赠送还是出售。然而，对于仅注重创作过程或数字使用的作品，耐光性则不那么关键。文章旨在帮助艺术家选择合适的材料，以确保作品的持久鲜艳。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同介质（如笔、颜料、纹身墨水）的耐光性和持久性

不同观点：
• smokel 分享了使用符合 ISO 12757-2 标准的档案墨水进行绘图的经验，发现这些绘图在一年内褪色。他指出，该标准适用于存档（如保存在盒子里），而非长期展示。同时提到 BIC 圆珠笔的蓝色墨水在阳光下会变黑。
• hoistbypetard 表示尽管对色素的耐光性没有直接兴趣，但觉得 smokel 的测试和研究非常有趣，并认为这些通常被视为个人审美偏好而非可量化指标。
• humblebeekeeper 从纹身墨水的角度参与讨论，指出紫外线会使纹身颗粒变小，并分享了与淋巴系统相关的有趣事实。
• mattgrice 详细讨论了不同颜色的耐光性，指出粉色和橙色通常不耐光，红色颜料如镉虽耐光但有毒。还提到了一些传统但易褪色的颜料如玫瑰红和茜素 crimson。
• burnt-resistor 对整个测试过程表示赞赏，称之为“艺术版的 Project Farm”。
• chris_st 提到一本关于水彩测试的书，并分享了自己在黑色笔耐光性测试中的经验，发现 Micron 笔具有耐光性。
• sllabres 分享了其对喷墨打印机墨水和保护膜的测试结果，发现红色墨水在 4 个月内褪色，而黑色墨水 20 年后仍保持较好。
• wrp 对机械铅笔芯进行了类似测试，推荐使用 Staedtler Mars Micro Color 以获得耐光性。
• dylan604 对粉色在测试图表中表现最差的现象表示好奇，想知道其实际视觉效果是否完全消失或仅是数据上接近于零。
• CGMthrowaway 提出天然颜料通常不如合成颜料耐光，并询问如果偏好天然颜料的色彩质量，是否选择测试中表现较差的铅笔是合理的。
• bayindirh 简短指出 Caran d'Ache 以其高品质和价格著称。
• __mharrison__ 表示曾认为 Prismacolors 是彩色铅笔的终极选择，对测试结果表示遗憾。
• hoppyhoppy2 提供了一个存档链接，指向一个关于光耐久性的网站。
• gennarro 对测试图片的质量和测试条件（如每天 6 小时阳光照射）表示质疑，并询问固定剂是否有助于测试。

补充讨论：
- 测试条件和方法的多样性，如不同的墨水、颜料、铅笔和保护膜。
- 天然与合成颜料的耐光性对比。
- 不同颜色（尤其是红色和粉色）在耐光性上的差异。
- 用户对品牌和价格的看法，如 Prismacolors 和 Caran d'Ache。
- 实际测试结果和标准（如 ISO 12757-2）之间的差距。
- 纹身墨水在紫外线下的变化作为一个有趣的跨领域讨论点。

44468753.article_content:
Lightfast Testing: 50+ Coloured Pencil Brands
By
Sarah Renae Clark
|
2025-04-22T16:47:32+10:00
April 5th, 2025
|
Have you ever spent hours on a piece of artwork, only to watch it fade over time? It’s a frustrating reality for many artists, and it all comes down to something called ‘lightfastness’ – a medium’s resistance to fading over time when exposed to light. If you want your work to last, choosing supplies with good lightfast ratings is essential.
But how do we know which art supplies will hold up over time? Some brands advertise their materials as “lightfast,” but do their claims hold up in real-world conditions? That’s exactly what I set out to test. Over the past 6 months, I’ve exposed swatches of coloured pencils and markers to sunlight and tracked their changes. I also compared my results to industry-standard lightfastness tests to see how different brands truly perform.
In this blog, I’ll break down:
What is Lightfastness?
Why Does it Matter?
How is Lightfastness Measured? And how I measured it.
My 6-month Lightfast Testing Results and Insights
Whether you’re a professional artist selling your work or a hobbyist who wants their art to last, this guide will help you make informed choices about your supplies.
>>> CLICK HERE TO JUMP TO THE RESULTS!
What is Lightfastness?
Lightfastness refers to how well a colour resists fading when exposed to light over time.
Art supplies that are “highly lightfast” can often last 100 years or more in museum conditions. While other art supplies might fade as soon as they see the sun. This is especially important for artists who want their work to last for years without significant colour shifts.
Fading occurs because some pigments break down when exposed to light, particularly ultraviolet (UV) rays from the sun. Different art supplies use different types of pigments and binding materials, which means some colours are naturally more resistant to fading than others. While some art materials are designed to be highly lightfast, others may start losing their vibrancy after just a few days of exposure to light.
Understanding lightfastness helps artists make better choices about their materials, whether they’re working on personal projects, commissions, or selling their art. In the next sections, we’ll explore why this matters and how it’s tested.
Why is Lightfastness Important?
Nobody wants to pour time and creativity into an artwork only to see it fade away. That’s why lightfastness (how well your colours resists fading over time) is worth paying attention to. Whether you’re colouring for fun, creating gifts, or selling your work, fading colours can be a letdown.
Art you want to display
If you enjoy displaying your artwork, lightfastness is something to consider. You probably want your art to stay true to its original colours. Artwork displayed in well-lit areas – especially near windows – can fade quickly if created with non-lightfast materials. Choosing the right supplies helps preserve your work so it can be enjoyed for years without noticeable fading or colour shifts.
Art you want to give away
If you love sharing your artwork with friends and family, lightfastness is something to consider. A beautifully coloured piece might look stunning at first, but if it starts to fade after a few months, it could lose its charm. Choosing lightfast materials ensures that your gifts remain as vibrant and meaningful as the day you gave them.
Art you want to sell
If you’re selling artwork, ensuring that your materials are lightfast is essential. Buyers expect their purchases to last, and if a piece fades within months or years, it can damage your reputation as an artist. Many professional artists specifically choose lightfast materials to guarantee their work remains vibrant for generations.
When is Lightfastness NOT Important?
Lightfastness isn’t always a top priority, and that’s completely okay! If your focus is on the process rather than the final piece, then fading might not matter to you at all. This includes things like:
Personal work where you’re experimenting, practising, or simply enjoying the creative flow.
Projects that you plan to scan or photograph the final piece and use it digitally or for prints rather than keeping the original.
Artwork that stays safely tucked away in a sketchbook or colouring book, away from sunlight.
In these cases, it makes perfect sense to use whatever tools you enjoy most, regardless of their lightfast rating.
Advertisement
Advertisement
How is Lightfastness Measured?
There are three main ways to measure how much a colour fades over time:
Blue Wool Scale
– An industry standard using blue-dyed wool strips that fade at different intervals. My testing is based on this method.
ASTM D6901
– A lab-based test for coloured pencils only, using controlled light exposure. Not suitable for markers.
Manufacturer Ratings
– Internal tests done by brands, which can vary in accuracy.
I talk about more of these in more detail in

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个地铁模拟项目的功能、设计、技术问题及实用性的多方面讨论

不同观点：
• **关于列车停留时间（dwell time）的合理性**：
  - [avianlyric] 认为默认的停留时间过短，特别是在高运力系统中，停留时间是限制乘客容量的关键因素。举例伦敦Victoria线的停留时间在24-30秒以上。并指出停留时间包括开关门、安全检查等多个环节，而不仅仅是乘客上下车。
  
• **关于技术实现的讨论**：
  - [avianlyric] 指出纽约地铁使用的是固定块系统，而不是移动块系统，后者更有效率，但实现难度大。
  - [xnx] 提到在编辑路线时遇到技术问题，点击按钮后出现控制台错误，页面空白。
  
• **关于用户界面和视觉设计的建议**：
  - [blehn] 对项目的视觉设计提出批评，认为颜色和状态指示不够直观，建议根据线路颜色进行匹配，并提出了一套动态视觉指示方案（不同状态不同透明度和填充颜色）。
  - [pimlottc] 指出该项目在手机端不友好，地图控件遮挡了大部分地图，建议增加控件最小化功能。

• **关于项目扩展性和适用性的讨论**：
  - [kiwibyproxy] 对项目表示赞赏，但希望有更多关于项目结构和如何适应其他城市的说明。
  - [shiroiuma] 质疑自定义路线设计的实用性，指出纽约不大可能建设新线路，暗示该功能可能仅供娱乐。
  
• **关于路线规划的实际应用讨论**：
  - [ars] 尝试设计从Bay Ridge到Clinton的路线，并延伸讨论到Staten Island到新泽西的公共交通匮乏问题，指出即使设计了新线路，实际实施也可能面临挑战（如需要扩建桥梁）。

补充讨论：
• **趣味性和潜在应用**：
  - [darthplagius] 表示会将该项目分享给MTA的创新团队，认为他们会感兴趣。
  - [Aaronstotle] 对项目表示兴奋，提到想设计穿越公园的地铁路线。
  
• **其他体验反馈**：
  - [fsckboy] 以幽默方式指出项目未模拟高峰时段车厢内的恶劣环境（如异味和积水）。
  - [zerojames] 和 [indoordin0saur] 对项目表示赞赏，认为其创意有趣。

争议焦点：
• **停留时间的合理性**：[avianlyric] 提出的停留时间过短的问题与其他用户对项目整体趣味性和创意的赞赏形成对比，显示出技术细节与娱乐性设计之间的张力。

补充讨论：
• **趣味性和潜在应用**：
  - [darthplagius] 表示会将该项目分享给MTA的创新团队，认为他们会感兴趣。
  - [Aaronstotle] 对项目表示兴奋，提到想设计穿越公园的地铁路线。
  
• **其他体验反馈**：
  - [fsckboy] 以幽默方式指出项目未模拟高峰时段车厢内的恶劣环境（如异味和积水）。
  - [zerojames] 和 [indoordin0saur] 对项目表示赞赏，认为其创意有趣。

争议焦点：
• **停留时间的合理性**：[avianlyric] 提出的停留时间过短的问题与其他用户对项目整体趣味性和创意的赞赏形成对比，显示出技术细节与娱乐性设计之间的张力。

data.title: SUS Lang: The SUS Hardware Description Language
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary:
SUS HDL 是一种硬件描述语言，相比 Verilog 和 VHDL，具有以下特点：  
1. **延迟计数**：编译器自动管理时序和流水线。  
2. **便于实验**：编译器跟踪设计细节并显示在编辑器中。  
3. **完全控制**：支持同步逻辑设计。  
4. **强大的元编程**：允许编译时代码执行以生成 LUT 等。  

SUS 的核心哲学是提供直观、简洁的语法来构建网表，不强制特定范式，但要求硬件设计为同步逻辑，不适合异步硬件设计。  

主要功能包括：  
- 生成变量和类型自由组合  
- 易于实现流水线  
- 通过接口分离流水线  
- 提供代码到网表的直接映射  
- 内置流水线语法和编译时错误提示  

未来计划包括类型安全、多时钟模块支持和形式验证集成等。SUS 不提供握手协议抽象和自动流水线功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于硬件描述语言（HDL）及其工具链（尤其是测试平台和验证工具）的现状与改进的讨论。

不同观点：
• [1024bees] 认为新的硬件描述语言在测试平台设计和集成方面缺乏考虑，现有的工具（如Verilator、cocotb、UVM）虽然能用，但涉及到跨语言操作和生成代码，体验不佳。他建议SUS语言如果能内置对测试平台的支持，并能与UVM或Verilator映射，将会更有趣。

• [randomNumber7] 认为硬件描述语言及其工具确实需要革新，但要与主流竞争非常困难。虽然承认问题存在，但似乎对新语言的出现持谨慎态度。

• [ForgotMyUUID] 更关注文档生成工具，尤其是针对Verilog/VHDL的API文档自动生成工具，类似于Sphinx中的autodoc功能。这代表了一部分开发者对文档工作流的关注。

• [mdhb] 提到了Intel的一个项目——ROHD框架，该框架允许在Dart编程语言中描述和验证硬件。这展示了现有硬件开发中的一种新方向，即通过其他编程语言来扩展硬件描述的能力。

• [artemonster] 作为RTL设计者，强烈反对引入新的“花哨”HDL。他认为现有的HDL已经足够好，真正的问题在于工具和验证流程的不足。他强调设计复杂性的瓶颈在于验证能力，而不是语言本身。

补充讨论：
• [hulitu] 和 [ei8ths] 的评论带有调侃性质，[hulitu] 对SUS的缩写产生疑问，[ei8ths] 则简单表达了对整个讨论主题的怀疑态度。

争议焦点：
• 是否需要新的硬件描述语言（如SUS）来改进测试平台设计和集成，还是专注于改进现有工具和流程（如UVM和Verilator）。[1024bees] 和 [artemonster] 的观点形成对比，前者希望看到语言层面的创新，而后者认为现有工具和语言足够，问题在于验证和工具链的不足。

• 硬件描述语言的未来发展方向：是通过引入新语言（如ROHD框架）来扩展能力，还是在现有语言基础上改进工具和工作流（如文档生成工具）。

Why SUS?
The SUS HDL stands out compared to other HDLs like Verilog or VHDL due to its:
⚡
Latency Counting
Timing and pipelining is easier to reason about because the compiler keeps track of them.
🛠️
Made for tinkering
The compiler keeps track of many aspects of your hardware design, and displays them in the editor.
🔒
Full Control
If you can draw your design as synchronous logic, you can represent it in SUS.
💡
Powerful Metaprogramming
SUS allows compile-time code execution to generate LUTs

Core Philosophy
The
SUS HDL
is meant to be a direct competitor to Synthesizeable Verilog and VHDL. Its main goal is to be an intuitive and
thin syntax for building netlists, such that traditional synthesis tools can still be used to analyze the
resulting hardware. SUS shall impose no paradigm on the hardware designer, such as requiring specific
communication protocols or iteration constructs. In other words, SUS is not there to abstract away complexity, but
rather to make the inherent complexity of hardware design more manageable.
The one restriction SUS does impose over Verilog and VHDL is that it requires the hardware to be synchronous over
one or more clocks. Asynchronous hardware is therefore unrepresentable making SUS less suitable for ASIC
development.
Main Features of SUS
Generative Variables and Types:
Can be freely combined, sidestepping any "Dependent
Types" headaches.
Easy Pipelining:
Achieved through an orthogonal construct called "Latency Counting"
that doesn't interfere with other features.
Separation of Pipelines:
Using interfaces to prevent crossing signals without logical
relationship.
What SUS Gives You
A direct 1-to-1 mapping from code to netlist
Hardware domain separation with explicit crossing primitives
A built-in syntax for pipelining that does not impose structural constraints
In-IDE compilation errors & warnings
Metaprogramming for hardware generation
Planned Features
Type safety with Bounded Integers
Multi-Clock modules
Formal Verification Integration
Syntactic sugar for common constructs like valid signals, resets and submodule communication
Moving some timing constraints to the source file
What SUS Does Not Do
Provide abstractions for handshake protocols (like AXI)
Runtime iteration constructs
Automatic pipelining & retiming

Watch an introductory video covering the basics of the language.

Connect with us on our platforms like GitHub or Discord.

data.title: Applite – A macOS native GUI for homebrew
data.author: napolux
data.article_summary: Applite是一款免费开源的应用程序管理工具，专为非技术用户设计，使用简单，通过单键操作即可下载、更新和卸载应用。它基于Homebrew包管理器，适用于macOS，用户可以选择使用现有Homebrew安装或为Applite创建新安装。Applite提供的应用均来自Homebrew Catalog，用户可通过搜索功能查找。虽然macOS内置安全机制会扫描应用安全性，但某些应用可能未被沙箱化，用户需谨慎。Applite本身不追踪任何信息，且所有操作透明。用户可通过DMG文件或Homebrew命令安装Applite。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Homebrew及其相关工具的看法和建议

不同观点：
• **exabrial** 认为Homebrew是一种理想的状态，无需账户、无需保持最新版本，并且可以安装任何想要的版本，比苹果的应用商店更好。
• **c-hendricks** 仅提到Homebrew Casks，没有展开具体观点。
• **egorfine** 指出标题有误导性，该工具并非Homebrew软件包的图形界面。
• **chuck8088** 对项目表示赞赏，并关注Homebrew安装过程中可能遇到的错误报告和调试问题，显示出对用户体验的关心。
• **giamma** 认为该工具不错，但建议增加显示软件描述、许可证信息以及是否为试用版的功能，以减少用户点击次数，提高效率。
• **Proofread0592** 关心安全问题，询问是否可以设置仅显示经过公证的Casks，以确保应用的安全性。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户如**exabrial** 和 **chuck8088** 对Homebrew的优点表示赞赏，但也隐含了对安装过程可能出现问题的关注。
• **giamma** 和 **Proofread0592** 提出了具体功能需求，关注用户体验和安全性，显示出用户对工具完善性的期望。
• **egorfine** 对工具的命名和功能描述提出了质疑，指出了潜在的误解。

争议焦点：
• 工具的命名和功能描述是否准确（**egorfine** 的观点），以及如何在工具中平衡用户体验（**giamma** 的建议）和安全性（**Proofread0592** 的问题）。

44489894.article_content:
Key Features
Download and manage with a single click
Download, update and uninstall apps with a single click
Clean and simple UI
Designed for non-technical users
Free and open-source
No costs, no tracking, fully transparent
Applite uses the
Homebrew
package manager under the hood. Homebrew is a free and open source project that
makes it easy to install developer tools and desktop applications on macOS.
What apps are available on Applite?
Any application that can be found in the
Homebrew Catalog
is available on Applite. Use the search function to find all applications in Applite.
Is it secure?
The macOS built-in protection (Gatekeeper and XProtect) will scan the application for potential malware
the first time you open it and notify you if anything is suspicious. Also, most applications in the Homebrew
Catalog are notarized, which means they come from a registered developer.
The apps may not be sandboxed, which allows them to affect your system with elevated privileges.
Nevertheless, be careful, as some applications may contain malware, especially those that have few downloads.
Applite itself is also not sandboxed.
What information does Applite track?
None.
Applite and Homebrew
Can I use Applite with my existing Homebrew installation?
Yes, you can. The first time you open the application, you will be asked if you want to use your own brew
or if you want to create a new installation just for Applite.
If you choose to create a new installation it will be stored at:
~/Library/Application Support/Applite/homebrew
.
Can I manage already installed apps with Applite?
If you chose to use your existing brew installation all casks installed with it will appear in Applite.
Any other apps installed manually (e.g. from DMG or PKG files) will not show up as installed in Applite.
You can add them by reinstalling them. See
troubleshooting
page
for more information on adding already installed apps.
Read the full FAQ for more information
.

data.title: The chemical secrets that help keep honey fresh for so long
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 蜂蜜因其特殊的化学性质和制作过程，具有极强的抗变质能力。蜜蜂在酿蜜过程中，通过去除花蜜中的水分并使用酶提高酸度，使得蜂蜜的含水量降至15%-18%，同时糖分高度浓缩。这种低水分高糖的环境抑制了微生物的生长。密封的蜂蜜限制了氧气接触，进一步防止变质。虽然蜂蜜可能会结晶，但在适当保存下不会变质。然而，开封后接触空气和污染物可能导致变质。这种抗腐能力使得蜂蜜被视为一种“神奇”的食品，类似于现代食品科学中的“低水分活性”保存法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：蜂蜜为何能长时间保持新鲜及其相关特性

不同观点：
• **Jun8的观点**：通过降低水分活度（aw），Nutella和蜂蜜等食品能够在不冷藏的情况下长时间保持新鲜。Nutella的aw约为0.4，蜂蜜的aw为0.5-0.6，而花生酱的aw为0.7，这些都使得它们能够较长时间保鲜。
• **YeGoblynQueenne的观点**：即使蜂蜜暴露在空气中并接触到细菌和湿气，它仍然不容易变质。基于个人经验，打开的蜂蜜罐即使放置多年也不会变质，虽然外观可能变得不吸引人。
• **bjelkeman-again的观点**：蜂蜜中常见的乳酸菌具有抗菌效果，能够抑制其他细菌的生长，这也是蜂蜜保持新鲜的原因之一。
• **cypherpunks01的观点**：蜂蜜中可能含有少量的肉毒杆菌，这种细菌会导致婴儿肉毒中毒，因此不建议给婴儿食用蜂蜜。
• **kragen的观点**：低水分活度和低pH值并不能完全解释蜂蜜惊人的保鲜能力。蜂蜜的保存性还与其含有葡萄糖氧化酶产生的葡萄糖酸和过氧化氢，以及甲基乙二醛等成分有关。

补充讨论：
• **__mharrison__的经验**：在急救培训中了解到蜂蜜可以帮助伤口更快愈合，并通过个人实验验证了这一说法。
• **RataNova的观点**：蜜蜂在数千年前就创造了一种生物化学保存系统，远早于人类建立食品科学实验室。
• **cryptonector的观点**：高糖浓度可以破坏简单生物的细胞，这也是蜂蜜能够保持新鲜的原因之一。
• **giantg2的观点**：蜂蜜保鲜的真正秘密在于其产生的高渗透压。
• **SeanDav的经验**：曾经养蜂，但因对蜂蜇过敏而不得不放弃。养蜂不仅有趣，还能对环境和食品生产做出贡献。

44463429.article_content:
The chemical secrets that help keep honey fresh for so long
6 days ago
Share
Save
Veronique Greenwood
Share
Save
Getty Images
Honey is a natural sweetener, and bacteria loves to feast on sugar. But honey is remarkably resistant to spoilage. What's behind its ability to beat the bugs?
Most jarred delights have a limited shelf life – they're just one mucky spoon dip away from growing a luscious crop of mould or a thriving colony of bacteria. But there are certain foods with peculiar staying power, capable of staying edible for years.
Honey is one of these magical substances. In a sealed environment, while the golden stuff may crystallise, turning thick and chunky,
it will not go off
. This persistent ability to resist decay is down to honey's chemistry, and the way in which it is made.
When we say that food has spoiled, what we actually mean is that
something else
has got to it first, something microscopic. Bacteria, fungi, and moulds
are present
in at least low numbers in many foods, and a number of the procedures humans use to preserve food are designed to discourage these creatures consuming it.
Alamy
Honey may crystallise when it is in a sealed jar, but it does not go off (Credit: Alamy)
Many of these microorganisms tend to prefer moist conditions, higher (but not too high) temperatures, a mellow pH, and plenty of oxygen around to use in their metabolism. Dehydrating meat or fruit, then, deprives them of water. Cooking food to a high heat and then moving it into the fridge for storage first kills off many bugs and puts a damper on the growth of any left behind. Suspending food in a pickling mixture wards off all but the most acid-loving creatures. Sealing something in a jar limits the oxygen they have access to.
We are always fighting a losing battle against these organisms
Even food that's been put through a gauntlet of preservation procedures usually has a limited shelf life, as you might know if you have ever opened a jar of butterscotch sauce from the back of grandma's fridge, sealed in 1985, to find a thick carpet of fuzz within. (Don't ask me how I know.)
We are always fighting a losing battle against these organisms, and whether it's a whiff of vinegar that tells us the
Lactobacillus
has had its way with the orange juice, or black mould spots on the inside wall of the peanut butter jar, the signs of their presence are often unsubtle, and unavoidable.
But honey is an unusual case, and here is why. It's made by honeybees from flower nectar, and starts out as a warmish, watery, sugary fluid, the kind of thing that seems like it would be the purest bacteria bait. The bees
concentrate the nectar
on the way to the hive, removing some of the water, use enzymes to raise the acid content in the fluid discouraging some forms of microorganisms from growing, and break down the sugars into simpler ones, then decant the stuff into honeycomb chambers.
Getty Images
Sealing honey in jars adds to the purifying procedures bees carry out, which massively reduces the water content (Credit: Getty Images)
Next, they do something remarkable: they start to fan the
honey with their wings
. The fanning slowly evaporates the remaining water, like an oscillating fan evaporating sweat from your skin, so a substance that was once about
70% or 80% water
sees that number drop and drop and drop.
Fully ripened honey typically has a water content between about
15% and 18%
. In fact, the proportion of sugar molecules to water is so enormous that it would not be physically possible to dissolve that much sugar into that much water, without a process like the one honeybees use.
More like this:
•
Bee gold: Why honey is an insect superfood
•
How to make fruit and vegetables last longer
•
The food that could last 2,000 years
There is plenty of sugar there, and of course microorganisms would love to have a go at it. But with so little water – and the acidity providing an additional disincentive – they simply can't survive. Seal honey in a jar, to limit the availability of oxygen, and there's another barrier to growth.
This is a state known as "low water activity" among food scientists, and in fact, lowering a substance's water activity is a common trick to preserve processed foods. It is possible to keep
moist food from spoiling as long as the water molecules are tied up in interactions with salt or sugar
, for example.
This doesn't mean that honey can withstand all challenges to freshness. Once a jar of honey is open, its surface is being regularly exposed to the air, and dipping licked spoons in will bring bacteria and moisture that weren't there when the jar was sealed.
But take charge of the situation by adding water, add your own specially chosen microorganism, and you get
mead
– a type of spoilage that few would argue with on a hot day, sitting in the shade.
--

44463429.article_summary: 蜂蜜因其特殊的化学性质和制作过程，具有极强的抗变质能力。蜜蜂在酿蜜过程中，通过去除花蜜中的水分并使用酶提高酸度，使得蜂蜜的含水量降至15%-18%，同时糖分高度浓缩。这种低水分高糖的环境抑制了微生物的生长。密封的蜂蜜限制了氧气接触，进一步防止变质。虽然蜂蜜可能会结晶，但在适当保存下不会变质。然而，开封后接触空气和污染物可能导致变质。这种抗腐能力使得蜂蜜被视为一种“神奇”的食品，类似于现代食品科学中的“低水分活性”保存法。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了宫脇方法（Miyawaki Method）这一微型森林种植技术，该方法通过种植本地树种，在短时间内打造密集的小型森林，已在全球范围内受到广泛关注。文章探讨了宫脇方法的创始人宫脇昭博士的遗产，以及该方法在不同地区的应用实例，如横滨国立大学和温哥华的Strathcona公园。尽管宫脇方法在绿化爱好者和政府中颇受欢迎，但专业生态学家对其效果的评价较少。文章还引用了多篇相关文献和案例研究，讨论了该方法的成功和争议。最后，文章邀请读者支持相关播客，以获取更多内容。

Cover artwork by Ale Silva
Summary
The Miyawaki Method of micro-forestry is a viral sensation: sprouting tiny, dense, native tree cover in neighbourhoods all around the world. With the promise of afforestation at a revolutionary speed, this planting technique has become the darling of green-space enthusiasts, industry, and governments alike — yet few professional or academic ecologists have commented on its efficacy, or even seem to have heard of it!
In this episode, we debate the legacy of Dr. Akira Miyawaki: the man, the myth, and the method.

data.title: AI cameras change driver behavior at intersections
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了人工智能（AI）摄像头在交通路口对驾驶员行为的改变及其潜在影响。这些摄像头能够实时监控和分析交通状况，通过警示系统或罚款机制减少闯红灯和超速等违规行为。作者指出，这些AI技术的应用有望降低交通事故死亡率，尤其是在高风险路口。尽管技术带来隐私担忧，但其安全效益不可忽视。文章强调，随着技术进步，AI在交通安全中的角色将愈加重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：交通执法、滚停（rolling stop）的合法性和安全性、交通基础设施设计与技术应用

不同观点：
• **支持滚停的观点**：SoftTalker认为在视线良好且没有行人或交叉交通的情况下，滚停并无不妥。其核心论据是，交通标志的目的是确保安全有序的交通流动，如果司机减速并确认安全，即使没有完全停下，目的也已经达到。

• **交通执法与安全比较的观点**：maeln指出美国交通事故死亡率远高于欧盟，表明需要对交通执法、基础设施设计和司机心态进行改革，暗示严格执法可能是必要的。

• **交通灯和交通流量管理的观点**：hlws提到交通灯不仅是为安全设计，也是为交通流量管理服务。在其居住地，许多司机将红灯视为建议而非强制，导致其他街道的严重堵塞问题。

• **技术替代与交通设计的观点**：grogenaut建议利用技术，如车内提示灯或智能交通灯，以替代传统的停车标志，从而更有效地管理交通流量，并减少对司机的干扰。

• **执法公平性与社会问题的观点**：pj_mukh指出其城市对无牌车辆缺乏执法，导致社会问题如肇事逃逸频发，质疑交通执法摄像头的实际效果和社会公平性。

• **"零愿景"目标的现实性观点**：SoftTalker对"零愿景"（Vision Zero）持怀疑态度，认为完全消除交通死亡是不现实的目标，资源分配应更加合理。

• **自动化执法的可行性观点**：djoldman认为技术并非推行自动化交通执法的障碍，而是公众接受度和运营成本问题。

• **历史经验与执法成本的观点**：mullingitover提到过去加州因运营成本高而放弃自动化交通执法系统，指出人类参与审核可降低误报率，但增加运营费用。

• **执法动机与长期影响的观点**：thrill和JohnMakin都质疑执法背后的动机，认为一旦某种执法手段成为收入来源，其废除将面临困难，且可能被滥用于其他目的，如数据收集和监控。

• **交通控制设备的实际效果与安全问题观点**：mindslight批评严格执行交通控制设备的“安全”措施，认为其分散司机注意力，可能导致更多事故，并指出改造交叉路口的昂贵成本。

补充讨论：
• **执法对驾驶行为的影响**：webdevver提到警察在场时司机行为的变化，暗示执法可能导致不必要的交通减速。

• **执法设备的真实目的**：chasd00直接质疑执法设备的真实目的，认为其主要是为了增加罚单收入而非提升交通安全。

争议的焦点：
• **滚停的合法性与安全性**：是否在特定条件下允许滚停，以及如何平衡司机便利性和交通安全。
• **自动化执法的公平性与有效性**：自动化执法技术的应用是否真正提高交通安全，还是仅仅成为政府的收入来源。
• **交通基础设施设计的成本与效果**：是否应投资改造现有交通基础设施以提升安全性与效率，还是依赖技术手段解决。

这些观点和讨论展示了交通执法、技术应用和基础设施设计之间的复杂关系，以及公众对交通安全和管理措施的不同看法。

data.title: LookingGlass: Generative Anamorphoses via Laplacian Pyramid Warping
data.author: jw1224
data.article_summary: 《LookingGlass: Generative Anamorphoses via Laplacian Pyramid Warping》一文介绍了一种生成变形图像的新方法。传统变形图像（anamorphosis）需从特定视角观察才能显现真实形态，而该文通过使用潜在校正流模型（latent rectified flow models）和拉普拉斯金字塔扭曲（Laplacian Pyramid Warping）技术，使得生成的图像即使直接观看也具有有效的视觉解释。该方法提升了图像的生成质量，并将视觉谜题（Visual Anagrams）扩展到潜在空间模型和更广泛的空间变换中，创造出新颖的生成感知错觉。文章发表于CVPR 2025。
data.comments_summary:

  - [mg] 提到正在进行的一个项目，通过交换短视频序列中最后一张图像的相邻像素，使其 resembling 第一张图像，并分享了相关示例。
  - [quitit] 回应并提供了其他类似项目的链接，扩展了关于图像处理技术的讨论。

• **技术应用的潜在可能性**：
  - [ygritte] 认为该技术可以用于隐写术（steganography），指出需要合适的镜像形式来进行解码。

• **对技术复兴的感慨**：
  - [fudged71] 表达了对许多光学错觉被新一代生成技术重新探索的喜爱。

44495154.article_content:
LookingGlass: Generative Anamorphoses via Laplacian Pyramid Warping
In this work, we revisit these famous optical illusions with a generative twist. With the help of latent rectified flow models, we propose a method to create anamorphic images that still retain a valid interpretation when viewed directly.
June 10, 2025
CVPR 2025
Authors
Pascal Chang (DisneyResearch|Studios/ETH Joint PhD)
Sergio Sancho (DisneyResearch|Studios/ETH Joint PhD)
Jingwei Tang (DisneyResearch|Studios)
Markus Gross (DisneyResearch|Studios)
Vinicius Azevedo (DisneyResearch|Studios)
LookingGlass: Generative Anamorphoses via Laplacian Pyramid Warping
Download Publication PDF
Download Supplemental PDF
Abstract
Anamorphosis refers to a category of images that are intentionally distorted, making them unrecognizable when viewed directly. Their true form only reveals itself when seen from a specific viewpoint, which can be through some catadioptric device like a mirror or a lens. While the construction of these mathematical devices can be traced back to as early as the 17th century, they are only interpretable when viewed from a specific vantage point and tend to lose meaning when seen normally. In this paper, we revisit these famous optical illusions with a generative twist. With the help of latent rectified flow models, we propose a method to create anamorphic images that still retain a valid interpretation when viewed directly. To this end, we introduce Laplacian Pyramid Warping, a frequency-aware image warping technique key to generating high-quality visuals. Our work extends Visual Anagrams to latent space models and to a wider range of spatial transforms, enabling the creation of novel generative perceptual illusions.

本文是关于作者在开源1U可管理以太网交换机项目（LATENTRED）中使用VSC8512 PHY芯片的经历。作者最初选择VSC8512是因为其QSGMII接口和 supposedly 完全公开的 datasheet，但在尝试调整SERDES TX均衡器设置时发现需要访问“机密参考手册”，该手册受NDA限制。由于无法签署NDA，作者只能依赖公开文档解决问题。

公开文档包括VSC8512 datasheet、硬件设计清单、IBIS-AMI模型和参考设计指南等。通过分析，作者发现VSC8512像是精简版交换机ASIC，并确认了一些SERDES参数（如OB_LEV、OB_PREC等），尽管不完全知道如何设置这些参数。作者还提到MESA API是一个有价值的信息来源，但文档不完善。最终，作者依靠有限的信息和实验解决了信号完整性问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：嵌入式开发中与硬件制造商相关的文档和工具发布的透明度问题，以及具体厂商（如Microchip和Texas Instruments）在开放资源和收费策略上的不同做法。

不同观点：
• ACCount36强烈批评硅厂商拒绝发布完整的文档和工具，认为这是嵌入式开发中最令人讨厌的问题之一。
• gregfjohnson对Microchip的IDE MPLAB X v6.20进行了讨论，指出其基于gcc编译器，但优化功能需支付1000美元的许可费。他认为这可能违反了gcc的copyleft许可证，并考虑向EFF举报。
• anitil欣赏该系列文章，指出硬件开发的困难在于制造商不总是完全公开或诚实 about 设备能力，通常在开发深入后才被发现。
• 0xTJ希望Microchip能正式发布Atmel ATF系列可编程算法和位图，尽管部分已被逆向工程，但官方公开会更好。
• lttlrck提到令牌环技术在1996年已过时，但推测某些工业系统可能仍需与其接口，导致其在"暗硅"中存留。
• hwj赞扬Texas Instruments的文档详细，尤其是MSP430微控制器的完整指南和错误指南，并指出Clang默认支持MSP430。
• userbinator认为Microchip在开放收购自其他公司的资源上做得不错，例如Atmel的安全IC现在有完整的数据表可免费下载。
• kragen对文章的综合性和无畏表示赞赏，特别提到作者Andrew Zonenberg。
• nemo8551喜欢该系列文章，并请求推荐类似深度分析内容。
• Taniwha和RainyDayTmrw的评论更侧重于对特定术语或现象的简短看法，未提出新的论点。

补充讨论：
• 关于Microchip收费策略是否违反gcc的copyleft许可证存在争议，gregfjohnson考虑举报，但尚未确定是否有法律漏洞。
• 对不同厂商（Microchip和Texas Instruments）在文档和工具开放性上的表现有不同看法，部分用户如hwj认为Texas Instruments的文档做得很好。
• 讨论中提到了对逆向工程和公开文档的需求，特别是对特定设备编程算法的官方发布呼声较高。

争议焦点：Microchip的收费优化功能是否违反gcc的copyleft许可证。

44468718.article_content:
Switch project, part 3 - what Microchip doesn't (officially) tell you about the VSC8512
2025-07-04 08:00
This is part 3 of my ongoing series about LATENTRED, my project to create an open source 1U managed Ethernet switch
from scratch.
Hereâs a quick, or maybe not-so-quick, update about the PHY on the line card and some of my troubles (and solutions).
And probably more internal details than you want to know, but hey - maybe this will be useful to somebody. Not a lot of pretty pictures either. One day I do want to decap one for fun, but I have better things to do with my time than try to fully netlist-extract a large 65nm IC just to figure out some undocumented registers.
Background
I chose the VSC8512 as the PHY for the line card because it had a QSGMII interface (which used much less pins than SGMII), but also (so I thought) had a fully open datasheet with no NDAs required.
Typically Iâm used to seeing parts that are either fully NDAâd (with a trivial product brief and no register info etc, or sometimes not even pinout info, public), or fully open. Sometimes I find components with specific documents restricted, but itâs almost always clear that âthis document/ref design exists, you canât get it without an NDA, but we are openly telling you weâre holding it backâ.
In my previous post I mentioned that there was no documentation for how to change the SERDES TX equalizer settings on the PHY side of the QSGMII. I opened a support case and Microchip responded saying that additional info was available in the âconfidential reference manualâ for the part which required an NDA. The rest of the reply was pretty generic and mentioned indirect register access but no specifics.
I was quite annoyed at this, as I had specifically chosen the part believing there was no restricted documentation. Since signing an NDA wasnât an option, it seemed I had the choice of suboptimal signal integrity or figuring things out from the limited public information. The eye was still reasonably open as-is and my cables and boards didnât have a ton of insertion loss, so worst case things would probably work with the default TX config.
But why would I settle for bad SI when I could read a bunch of poorly documented code and datasheets deliberately missing details?
What we have to go on
So, we know there is a confidential reference manual. But thereâs a lot of docs available to the public - after all, I was able to make a board, bring up the PHY, and pass packets without it.
VSC8512 datasheet (VMDS-10396). This is 139 pages of meat including what I thought was a complete set of registers.
VSC8512 hardware design checklist (DS00004697A)
VSC8504 Serdes6G IBIS-AMI model. This is for the 4-port version of the same PHY but is linked on the product web page; presumably the 04 and 12 use the same IP.
VSC742x / 85x2 reference design guide (UG1037). This describes a 24-port switch reference design using a SparX-III / Caracal switch ASIC (including 12 integrated PHYs) paired with a VSC85x2. Not a ton interesting here.
Microchip Ethernet Switch API (MESA), MIT licensed HAL for Microchip/Vitesse PHYs and switches available on GitHub. As youâll see in a bit, this is an absolute gold mine of information but itâs (perhaps intentionally) not well documented what a lot of the bitfields and APIs do.
Initial observations
Itâs pretty easy to see that the VSC8512 is a nerfed switch ASIC. Thereâs an entire DDR I/O controller thatâs unused (over a dozen VDD_IODDR pins youâre instructed to ground, plus a large group of NC pins in the surrounding area). So docs for the un-crippled switch ASIC, which I suspected and later confirmed was the VSC742x, are potentially of interest too.
The IBIS-AMI model included the magic name âSerdes6Gâ. Searching for this turned up some additional docs, most notably AN3743 (DS00003743A) which purports to be about the VSC74xx / 84xx but seems to be describing something very similar to whatâs on the 8512.
Between the various documents I was able to conclude that the VSC8512 is made on an unspecified 65nm process (I should decap one at some point and figure out whose / see what it looks likeâ¦ Luton first stepping is mentioned as being fabbed at TSMC in
vtss_phy_do_page_chk
so I suspect the rest are as well).
The SERDES macro was developed by the âGerman Design Centerâ (in the Dortmund area, according to some LinkedIn hits from a google search) - interesting to know, but not particularly useful in this context.
The IBIS model describes some very useful parameters. We donât know how to actually set them yet, but we know they exist, their ranges, and (most importantly) their names:
OB_LEV
: amplitude / main cursor tap, 0 to 63
OB_PREC
: pre-cursor FFE tap, -15 to +15
OB_POST0
: post cursor 0 FFE tap, -31 to +31
OB_POST1
: post cursor 1 FFE tap, -15 to +15
OB_POL
: output invert
OB_SER_H
: coarse slew rate adjust (slow/fast)
OB_SER
: fine slew rate adjust, 0 to 15

data.title: Charles Babbage and deciphering codes (1864)
data.author: pncnmnp
data.article_summary: 查尔斯·巴贝奇（Charles Babbage）在1864年出版的自传《一个哲学家的生命历程》（*Passages from the Life of a Philosopher*）中，讨论了破译密码的艺术。他从小就对解码感兴趣，在学生时代就能破解高年级学生制作的简单密码。巴贝奇认为，破译密码是一项需要时间、创造力和耐心的工作，很少有密码值得花费精力去破解。他提到，许多人都相信自己能创造出无法被破解的密码，但往往这种信念是错误的。巴贝奇曾与皇家学会主席戴维斯·吉尔伯特（Davies Gilbert）讨论过不可破解的密码，然而他们设想的密码最终都被成功破译。巴贝奇描述了一种基于同心圆的密码系统，内圈和外圈的字母排列不同，但通过仔细分析和推理，他依然能够破解此类密码。这表明，即便是复杂的密码，也难以做到完全不可破译。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Babbage及现代密码学相关的讨论

不同观点：
• **[evanjrowley]** 推荐了William Gibson的《The Difference Engine》一书，认为这本书适合对该话题感兴趣的读者。他提供了一个扩展阅读的建议，将讨论引向文学作品，但并未直接讨论Babbage的思想或现代密码学。

• **[Fethbita]** 表示对Babbage关于密码分析的思想很感兴趣，并表达了对Babbage如何看待现代密码学的愿望。这显示出对历史人物与现代技术发展之间联系的关注，尤其是对Babbage未能见证现代密码学进步的遗憾。

补充讨论：
- **扩展阅读的建议**：[evanjrowley]提供的书籍链接将讨论延伸到了科幻文学领域，尤其是与Babbage所处时代相关的蒸汽朋克风格作品。
- **历史与现代技术的结合**：[Fethbita]的观点突出了对历史人物在现代技术背景下的思考，特别是密码学领域的古今对比，涉及了人们对技术演进的好奇心。
- **未有直接争议**：两位评论者之间没有直接的争议，更多是不同关注点的表达，一个侧重文学扩展，另一个侧重技术历史的好奇。

44466143.article_content:
Charles Babbage and deciphering codes
Charles Babbage wrote an autobiography
Passages from the Life of a Philosopher
which was published in London in
1864
. In our biography of Babbage we have quoted several passages from the book which tell us about his life and the analytical engine. Here we quote from Chapter XVIII of the book where Babbage writes about deciphering. What we present here is only an extract. In fact we omit a more technical part which describes the considerable effort that he had put in constructing dictionaries with particular properties to assist in deciphering:-
Deciphering is, in my opinion, one of the most fascinating of arts, and I fear I have wasted upon it more time than it deserves. I practised it in its simplest form when I was at school. The bigger boys made ciphers, but if I got hold of a few words, I usually found out the key. The consequence of this ingenuity was occasionally painful: the owners of the detected ciphers sometimes thrashed me, though the fault really lay in their own stupidity.
There is a kind of maxim amongst the craft of decipherers ..., that every cipher can be deciphered.
I am myself inclined to think that deciphering is an affair of time, ingenuity, and patience; and that very few ciphers are worth the trouble of unravelling them.
One of the most singular characteristics of the art of deciphering is the strong conviction possessed by every person, even moderately acquainted with it, that he is able to construct a cipher which nobody else can decipher. I have also observed that the cleverer the person, the more intimate is his conviction. In my earliest study of the subject I shared in this belief, and maintained it for many years.
In a conversation on that subject which I had with the late Mr Davies Gilbert, President of the Royal Society, each maintained that he possessed a cipher which was absolutely inscrutable. On comparison, it appeared that we had both imagined the same law, and we were thus confirmed in our conviction of the security of our cipher.
Many years after, the late Dr Fitton, having asked my opinion of the possibility of making an inscrutable cipher, I mentioned the conversation I had had with Davies Gilbert, and explained the law of the cipher, which we both thought would baffle the greatest adept in that science. Dr Fitton fully agreed in my view of the subject; but even whilst I was explaining the law, an indistinct glimpse of defeating it presented itself vaguely to my imagination. Having mentioned my newly-conceived doubt, it was entirely rejected by my friend. I then proposed that Dr Fitton should write a few sentences in a cipher constructed according to this law, and that I should make some attempts to unravel it. I offered to give a few hours to the subject; and if I could see my way to a solution, to continue my researches; but if not on the road to success, to tell him I had given up the task.
Late in the evening of that day I commenced a preparatory inquiry into the means of unravelling this new cipher, and I soon arrived at a tolerable certainty that I should succeed. The next night, on my return from a party, I found Dr Fitton's cipher on my table. I immediately commenced my attempt. After some time I found that it would not yield to my means of treating it; and on further examination I succeeded in proving that it was not written according to the law agreed upon. At first my friend was very positive that I was mistaken; and having taken it to his sister, by whose aid it was composed, he returned and told me that it was constructed upon the very law I had proposed. I then assured him that they must have made some mistake, and that my evidence was so irresistible, that if my life depended upon the result I should have no hesitation in making my election.
Dr Fitton again retired to consult his sister; and after the lapse of a considerable interval of time again returned, and informed me that I was right - that his sister had inadvertently mistaken the enunciation of the law. I now remarked that I possessed an absolute demonstration of the fact I had communicated to him; and added that, having conjectured the origin of the mistake, I would decipher the cipher with the erroneous law before he could send me the new cipher to be made according to the law originally proposed. Before the evening of the next day both ciphers had been translated.
This cipher was arranged upon the following principle: - Two concentric circles of cardboard were formed, each divided into twenty-six or more divisions.
On the outer were written in regular order the letters of the alphabet. On the inner circle were written the same twenty-six letters, but in any irregular manner.
In order to use this cipher, look for the first letter of the word to be ciphered on the outside circle. Opposite to it, on the inner circle, will be another letter, which is to be written as the cipher for the former.

data.title: Researchers Found a Better Way to Teach Large Language Models New Skills
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 研究人员开发了一种新技术，称为WeGeFT，显著提升了大型语言模型在特定任务（如常识推理、算术推理、指令跟随、代码生成和视觉识别）上的表现，且无需增加微调所需的计算能力。传统上，大型语言模型经过预训练后能够处理广泛的任务，但在特定领域表现欠佳，需要微调。WeGeFT基于2022年推出的LoRA技术，通过识别模型已熟悉的参数和需要学习的参数，重点调整后者，从而提高效率。实验证明，WeGeFT在多个任务上的表现优于或等于LoRA及其变体，同时不增加计算需求。研究团队还计划利用WeGeFT改进模型的安全性。该研究将在国际机器学习大会上发表。

主要讨论点：论文评审与讨论

不同观点：
• 支持论文的创新性：有评论者（如ferrariwidjaja）认为该论文提出的方法具有创新性，特别是在解决特定问题上提供了新的视角和工具。评论者强调了论文中模型设计和实验结果的亮点。

• 对论文方法的质疑：另一位评论者（如mhjabreel）对论文中使用的方法提出了质疑，认为某些假设条件在实际应用中可能不成立，影响了模型的实用性。该评论者还指出，论文缺乏对方法局限性的充分讨论。

• 实验设计的批评：有评论者（如mkioutov）认为论文中的实验设计存在缺陷，特别是在数据集的选择和实验条件的控制上不够严谨，可能导致结果的偏差。该评论者建议增加更多对比实验以增强说服力。

• 对理论深度的期望：一位评审（如lopezdiaz）提到，虽然论文在应用方面有贡献，但在理论深度上稍显不足，期望能看到更多关于方法背后理论基础的详细阐述。

News Releases
Researchers Found a Better Way to Teach Large Language Models New Skills
July 7, 2025
Matt Shipman
3-min. read
Image credit: Growtika.
For Immediate Release
Tianfu Wu
tianfu_wu@ncsu.edu
Matt Shipman
matt_shipman@ncsu.edu
Researchers have developed a technique that significantly improves the performance of large language models without increasing the computational power necessary to fine-tune the models. The researchers demonstrated that their technique improves the performance of these models over previous techniques in tasks including commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, instruction following, code generation, and visual recognition.
Large language models are artificial intelligence systems that are pretrained on huge data sets. After pretraining, these models predict which words should follow each other in order to respond to user queries. However, the nonspecific nature of pretraining means that there is ample room for improvement with these models when the user queries are focused on specific topics, such as when a user requests the model to answer a math question or to write computer code.
“In order to improve a model’s ability to perform more specific tasks, you need to fine-tune the model,” says Tianfu Wu, co-corresponding author of a paper on the work and an associate professor of computer engineering at North Carolina State University. “However, these models are so large that it is not feasible to re-train the entire model. Instead, you want to determine the smallest number of changes necessary to improve the model’s performance. We’ve developed a technique, called WeGeFT (pronounced
wee-gift
), that represents a significant advance for fine-tuning these large models.”
The big break-through for fine-tuning these large models was called LoRA, which came out in 2022. LoRA works by using mathematical tools to identify a small subset of key parameters that are most likely to improve a model’s performance on a specific task. There have been many attempts to improve upon LoRA, but Wu and his collaborators found these previous efforts either required significantly more computational power to improve performance, or used the same amount of computing power without improving performance.
“WeGeFT builds on LoRA, but incorporates additional mathematical tools that allow us to determine which of the key parameters the model is already familiar with and which parameters the model would need to ‘learn,’” says Wu. “By placing more weight on the truly novel parameters, we are able to improve model performance compared to LoRA without incorporating significant new computational demands.”
In proof-of-concept testing, the researchers found that WeGeFT performed as well as or better than LoRA and its many variants across a variety of downstream tasks: commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, instruction following, code generation, and visual recognition.
“We think this is a valuable step forward,” Wu says. “We are now exploring ways that WeGeFT could also be used to identify elements of the model that are responsible for harmful outputs, with the goal of improving AI alignment and ‘surgery’ to improve model safety and outputs. We expect that work to be forthcoming.”
The paper, “
WeGeFT: Weight-Generative Fine-Tuning for Multi-Faceted Efficient Adaptation of Large Models
,” will be presented July 17 at the International Conference on Machine Learning, being held in Vancouver, Canada. Co-corresponding author of the paper is Chinmay Savadikar, a Ph.D. student at NC State. The paper was co-authored by Xi Song, an independent researcher.
This work was done with support from the National Science Foundation under grants 1909644, 2024688 and 2013451; and from the Army Research Office under grants W911NF1810295 and W911NF2210010.
-shipman-

Fine-tuning large pretrained Transformer models can focus on either introducing a small number of new learnable parameters (parameter efficiency) or editing representations of a small number of tokens using lightweight modules (representation efficiency). While the pioneering method LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) inherently balances parameter, compute, and memory efficiency, many subsequent variants trade off compute and memory efficiency and/or performance to further reduce fine-tuning parameters. To address this limitation and unify parameter-efficient and representation-efficient fine-tuning, we propose Weight-Generative Fine-Tuning (WeGeFT, pronounced wee-gift), a novel approach that learns to generate fine-tuning weights directly from the pretrained weights. 44492970.article_summary: 研究人员开发了一种新技术，称为WeGeFT，显著提升了大型语言模型在特定任务（如常识推理、算术推理、指令跟随、代码生成和视觉识别）上的表现，且无需增加微调所需的计算能力。传统上，大型语言模型经过预训练后能够处理广泛的任务，但在特定领域表现欠佳，需要微调。WeGeFT基于2022年推出的LoRA技术，通过识别模型已熟悉的参数和需要学习的参数，重点调整后者，从而提高效率。实验证明，WeGeFT在多个任务上的表现优于或等于LoRA及其变体，同时不增加计算需求。研究团队还计划利用WeGeFT改进模型的安全性。该研究将在国际机器学习大会上发表。

主要讨论点：关于可验证随机性来源及其应用的讨论

不同观点：
• [grokgrok] 认为多个政府机构同步使用相同的随机源可能导致不良后果，例如同时收到陪审团义务、税务审计和征兵通知，暗示这种集中化的随机性管理存在潜在问题。

• [wuiheerfoj] 对可验证的量子随机性表示兴趣，并提到另一个使用传统加密技术的可验证随机性信标（drand.love），支持使用技术上更先进和可信的随机性来源。

• [Cshelton] 以幽默方式评论，提到使用实际事件（如Ralphie的跑步）作为真实随机性的来源，暗示对某些随机性来源的信任问题。

• [CaliforniaKarl] 关注API的兼容性问题，希望新的随机性信标能使用与NIST信标相同的API，以提高互操作性。

• [spelunker] 表示对随机性来源的物理原理感兴趣，特别是对不熟悉物理学的用户，提供了一个学习资源链接。

• [Octokat] 仅发表简短评论，无明确观点。

• [wslh] 推荐了解Twine Protocol，认为其在时间戳信任基础上创建的无共识层区块链可能有参考价值，暗示区块链技术在随机性应用中的潜力。

• [tonnydourado] 以幽默方式回应，无明确观点。

• [ribcage] 强烈反对依赖外部随机性网站，认为每台计算机都能生成随机性，质疑信任此类网站的必要性。

• [ntnsndr] 提出区块链技术的应用场景问题，暗示对区块链技术在随机性领域应用的兴趣或质疑。

补充讨论：
- 不同评论者对随机性来源的信任和技术实现有不同看法，部分关注具体技术实现和兼容性，部分则对实际应用场景和信任问题提出质疑。
- 评论中涉及的技术包括量子随机性、传统加密技术和区块链技术，显示出对多种技术路径的探讨。
- 争议的焦点在于是否应信任第三方提供的随机性来源以及如何在实际应用中实现随机性的可验证性和安全性。

data.title: Epanet-JS
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: EPANET-js是一款结合现代网络地图和行业标准EPANET液压模拟算法的网页应用，旨在帮助规划和更新供水系统。该工具由Iterating团队开发，利用了Tom MacWright之前发布的开放源代码工具Placemark，并对其进行了改进，甚至将核心库也进行了开源。EPANET-js与传统昂贵且局限于Windows的软件形成鲜明对比，提供了更便捷、成本更低的解决方案。通过使用WASM引擎，用户可以在浏览器中进行完整的模拟。这一项目不仅展示了开放源代码的价值，还为液压模拟领域提供了创新工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：EPANET hydraulic modelling软件的商业化与开源方案之间的对比，以及epanet-js项目的功能与定价模式。

不同观点：
• **lbutler的观点**：认为Autodesk和Bentley等商业软件公司在使用EPANET引擎时，没有回馈开源社区，且其软件价格昂贵、功能复杂。epanet-js项目旨在平衡免费软件与商业软件的功能，提供较为低价的解决方案（比商业软件便宜约90%），同时保持部分高级功能在两年后开源。

• **xnx的观点**：支持epanet-js，认为其作为浏览器中运行的免费工具，相比昂贵的传统软件（如Autodesk和Bentley的产品）是一个巨大的改进，体现了自由软件的优势，即便自己用不到，也觉得这个项目很酷。

• **bilekas的观点**：对项目的**Functional Source License (FSL)**表示不解，想知道为何要在两年后才完全转为MIT开源许可证。

• **stared的观点**：提出是否可以利用epanet-js创建类似SimCity的浏览器游戏，探讨了该工具的潜在用途。

• **jannes的观点**：关注epanet-js是否可以用于小规模场景（如家庭花园的灌溉系统），对软件在小规模模拟中的应用表示兴趣。

• **jalk的观点**：质疑目前市政使用的GIS系统是否已经包含所有必要的模拟功能（如污水、水管、电缆等），还是缺乏模拟部分的功能。

• **PoissonVache的观点**：质疑epanet-js的商业模式，建议可以采用更低的月费（如20美元/月），并询问项目作者是否因为所在公司使用昂贵软件而希望降低费用，同时对开源的长期目标表示好奇。

• **vinnymac的观点**：对epanet-js在老旧手机上运行良好表示赞赏，尽管该软件的移动支持仍在预览阶段。

• **iachilo的观点**：之前未听说过EPANET，也不知道饮用水系统有专门的软件，认为这个发现是很有价值的知识。

• **cab404的观点**：仅表示反对，未提供具体理由（"ne doljno!" 意为 "should not"）。

补充讨论：
• epanet-js通过将EPANET引擎转换为WASM，实现了在浏览器中运行的全模拟功能，并提供了相关源代码和应用链接，体现出对开源和透明度的重视。
• 价格比较：Autodesk和Bentley的软件每年费用高达$10k-$16k，而epanet-js提供类似功能但价格仅为其10%，并且提供免费使用的选项。
• 用户对epanet-js的潜在用途（如游戏开发、小规模灌溉系统设计）表现出兴趣，同时也对其开源许可模式和商业模式提出了一些疑问和建议。

争议焦点：
• epanet-js的定价和开源许可模式（FSL转MIT）引发了一些用户的好奇和疑问，部分用户希望了解更多细节和理由。
• 商业化软件的高价与开源方案的功能对比是另一个隐含的争议点。

44464628.article_content:
epanet-js
epanet-js
is a new web application that combines modern web maps with the industry-standard
EPANET
hydraulic simulation algorithm. It’s for people planning and updating water utility systems: connecting pipes and pressures and figuring out what will happen. It’s a problem area that I’m totally fascinated by and know very little about. It’s made by the folks from
Iterating
- Luke Butler and Sam Payá, who are experts in the field.
If you’ve been following along with my blog and projects, you might notice something familiar about this screenshot of epanet-js:
Yep! A lifetime ago, I built a company and product called
Placemark
, which was a tool for creating and editing map data. When the business part didn’t work out, I published a
free-to-use version of Placemark
and
made the code open source
. I chose a very permissive license for the code:
the MIT license
. I wanted to let
anything
happen, including -
especially
- people creating paid products with the code.
It’s hard to explain to people outside of the world of open source that folks building a business with the help of my code is
the dream
.
Partly it’s that ‘being helpful’ is one of the goals in life that never gets old. The other part is that
most software becomes obsolete and abandoned quickly
. Creating software with any legacy is rare and something to celebrate.
Plus, Placemark was a general purpose tool in search of a successful niche: I never figured out what that niche was. I had a lot of learning to do about product-market-fit. But hydraulic simulation is a real market, and these folks are real experts.
There are other markets like this, I’m sure, and using Placemark code as a base could be a good way to jumpstart those companies - it’s not perfect, as I’ve documented extensively, but it could be good as a first step.
And the folks at Iterating have even
contributed changes upstream to the open source Placemark
codebase, but that isn’t required by the MIT license at all: that’s just because they’re cool folks.
They’ve also
open sourced the core epanet-js library
, and released the web application
under the Functional Source License
, which
makes new code contributions open source after two years
.
</source>
And epanet-js is a tool that you can run in a browser - full simulations with a WASM-based engine. It’s competing with expensive old-school software that costs $16,000 a year, runs exclusively on Windows, is
priced by “pipes”
, and uses the same engine, EPANET. This is so much better in comparison. A radical improvement.
Congrats to Luke and Sam for creating
epanet-js
. It’s super cool. If you speak hydraulic simulation or know someone who does, try it out!
July 3, 2025
Tom MacWright
@macwright.com on Bluesky
,
@tmcw@mastodon.social on Mastodon

data.title: Why are there still 7 continents?
data.author: jppope
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了“大陆”的定义以及当前不同的大陆划分模型，如美国/西欧的7大洲模型、联合国的6大洲模型、俄罗斯的6大洲模型等，指出这些模型的划分标准并不一致且存在随意性。作者认为，欧洲被视为一个大陆更多是历史和文化因素所致，而非地理或地质上的合理性。作者提出一个基于地质特征、面积、隔离程度和人口的更一致的大陆划分标准，认为大陆应作为一种组织世界的工具，而不仅仅是历史遗留的概念。文章最后列举了一些明确应被视为大陆的区域，如亚洲、非洲、北美洲和南美洲，并对南极洲和澳大利亚是否应被视为大陆提出了看法。

44492888.article_content:
We've been teaching my kids about "the continents" and to the credit of my kid he asked me "what makes a continent?" Off the top of my head I didn't know precisely where the definition came from. I did however love the fact that my 5 year old has enough sense to ask why this thing is a thing. So I looked it up. Turns out the whole thing makes as much sense as a football bat.
Even after reading up on it I still can't figure out for the life of me why we have 7 continents. To be fair, when I say "we" I am talking about the American/ Western European model. There are other
models
, but they also feel pretty silly. Here are the most common continent models right now:
6 continents (The United Nations): Africa, Asia, Europe, "Americas", Antartica, Australia. This is taught mostly in Greece and Latin America according to wikipedia
6 continents (Russia/ Eastern Europe): Africa, Eurasia, Europe, North America, South America, Antartica, Australia
5 continent model: the 6 (UN) continent model but it just removes Antartica due to the fact that people don't live there.
5 continent model: A different 5 continent model just kinda says fuck it and starts combining things randomly (like Africa and Europe?)
4 continent model: cause why not?
And there is an 8 content model which arbitrarily includes Zealandia, a submerged landmass that is large, but its also only like ~700,000 square miles bigger than the indian sub-continent, has no people, isn't a tectonic plate.
Oddly,
the only pre-existing one that sort of makes sense to me is the 6-continent geological/ Russian model
. They have Africa, Eurasia, North America, South America, Antartica, and Austrailia. This is roughly a geological model. Presumably, they are the largest landmasses on tetonic plates. (See tectonic image below)
When I look at the status quo,
the obvious problem is Europe calling themselves a continent
, which is clearly a historic/ cultural legacy situation. Europe is on a contigous plate with Asia, its a relatively small landmass. If you are going to make Europe a continent and keep some level of intellectual consistency you definitely need to add the Indian subcontinent, and probably the Arabian Peninsula/ Greenland.
I think the Europeans are just using good old fashioned marketing by making all the important maps show Europe as larger than it really is...
When I look at the overall situation though,
I really don't hate Europe as a continent.
It's geographically separated from the other population centers on its tectonic plate, has a large enough landmass, and a large population.
What are continents anyway?
I think all the definitions kind of suck so lets say continents are an organizational tool that help to break down the world into more manageable pieces. By that definition the current models still suck, BUT we can likely build a more consistent model.
Building a better rubric
I get that arguing about the continents is about as useful as turn signals on a bmw. but here's my "I can build a bikeshed" model for you. Feel free to tell me its trash or improve it.
Geology
Separate geologic features such as tectonic plates, continental shelf, make up of the landmass.
Size
At a certain point the size of the landmass and divisibility is really what we're talking about here.
Distance and separation
How "distinct" is the thing. Kansas is a hard sell, but Madagascar is pretty darn separate.
Population
Since the continental model is mostly for organizing things, the population is actually a useful feature.
Definitely Continents

Separated from other contents (except potentially for Europe) by oceans. or narrow strips of land.

Basically separated from other continents by water

Basically separated from other continents by water

Probably Continents
Antartica
1 tectonic plate
5th largest landmass
14,200,000 km2 (5,500,000 sq mi)
Completely separated from other continents by oceans
5100 people (summer)
So the population element is really the only point of contention. Does a continent need a population? To me it feels like it shouldn't. When we nuke ourselves into a nuclear winter Antartica will still be just chillin'... Continents should be able to out last people.

data.title: SIMD.info – Reference tool for C intrinsics of all major SIMD engines
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: 这篇文章比较了几种不同的指令集架构（ISA），包括GO、VSX、NEON、SSE4.2、AVX2和AVX-512。这些指令集被广泛应用于不同的处理器中，以提升计算性能。GO是较新的实验性指令集，VSX主要用于IBM的Power架构，NEON是ARM处理器的SIMD指令集，擅长多媒体处理。SSE4.2是英特尔和AMD用于提升多媒体和数据处理能力的指令集。AVX2和AVX-512则是更高级的向量扩展指令集，支持更复杂的并行计算，尤其在科学计算和高性能计算中表现突出。不同的指令集适用于不同的应用场景，选择时需根据具体需求权衡性能和功耗。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SIMD参考文档的细节和搜索功能的实用性

不同观点：
• syockit：认为该网站的搜索功能不错，但指令细节不足，建议参考其他提供详细图解或伪代码的网站（如[2], [3], [4]），尤其是x86架构的处理方法。
• Const-me：指出该网站上的ISA扩展标签不准确，例如将SSE2、SSE3、SSSE3和SSE4.1的 intrinsics 都归为SSE 4.2，并且提到一个支持AVX2但不支持FMA3的处理器例子。
• fancyfredbot：提到使用Claude将标量代码转换为AVX512时遇到的问题，特别是处理嵌套的if语句和mask操作时。
• Sesse__：批评搜索结果过于 sparse，且包含不必要的描述和示例，同时对结果页面的可读性提出质疑。
• convery：认为搜索功能在没有明确指令时使用不便，例如搜索'SHA'无结果，而搜索'hash'得到不相关的结果。
• mshockwave：询问是否计划添加ARM SVE和RISC-V V扩展，表明对这些架构的兴趣。
• llm_nerd：认为SIMD工具虽然有趣且有智力上的回报，但大多数情况下使用合适的跨平台库更为实际。
• varispeed：表示希望看到MCUs上的SIMD支持。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于参考文档的细节和实用性，特别是与其他网站相比时的不足。
• 搜索功能的有效性和结果的相关性也引起了较多讨论，尤其是当用户不确定具体指令时遇到的困难。
• 对不同架构（如ARM、RISC-V、MCUs）的支持需求反映了用户对扩展功能的期待。
• llm_nerd的观点则引发了对直接使用SIMD指令与依赖库的实用性讨论。

data.title: # [derive(Clone)] Is Broken
data.author: RGBCube
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了Rust中自动派生 trait（如 `Clone`、`PartialEq` 等）的当前实现问题。具体来说，派生这些 trait 时，编译器要求所有泛型参数也必须实现对应的 trait，但这并不总是合理的。文章通过两个代码示例展示了这一问题：

1. 一个包含 `Arc` 的结构体在派生 `Clone` 时出错，因为编译器默认要求泛型参数 `T` 也实现 `Clone`，但实际上不需要。
2. 另一个示例展示了类似的问题，结构体 `WrapAlwaysEq` 包含一个泛型类型 `AlwaysEq`，在进行 `PartialEq` 和 `Eq` 比较时出现问题。

文章提出了两种解决方案：
1. 长期方案是提交RFC，进行讨论和稳定化，但这可能需要数年时间。
2. 短期方案是编写自定义宏来实现更灵活的派生逻辑，作者选择在 `derive_more` crate 中提出问题，并考虑创建新 crate。

最终，作者希望改进Rust中派生 trait 的实现方式，以避免不必要的泛型限制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust中自动派生的Clone trait是否存在问题及其处理方式

不同观点：
• **Clone派生是便利功能，复杂情况应手动实现**：loa_in_认为自动派生Clone是一种便利，但在派生实现不足时，应该手动编写自己的实现，而不是依赖自动派生。

• **所有泛型参数应强制要求Clone**：jhugo主张所有泛型参数都应默认实现Clone，因为无法假设它们不会被以需要克隆的方式使用。他认为这可能是Rust类型系统在1.0之前不够强大或只是一个被稳定化的疏忽。

• **Haskell的处理方式值得借鉴**：moomin提到Haskell在派生Eq时对泛型参数施加条件，认为Rust可以借鉴这种做法，以避免在未实现Clone的类型上使用时出现问题。

• **当前Clone派生机制足够清晰，无需复杂化**：xorvoid认为Rust中派生Clone的规则已经明确，虽然偶尔会导致合理代码被拒绝，但这是静态语言的共性，增加语言复杂性不值得。

• **应允许自定义界限**：kzrdude建议为derive(Clone)增加一个选项，以便更容易地自定义界限，明确指定需要的trait bounds。

• **现状简单且合理**：m3talsmith认为当前系统简单明了，不存在破损问题，未实现Clone的类型未编译通过是显而易见的。

• **无需对“复杂情况”进行更改**：bloppe质疑所谓“复杂情况”是否真的需要更改，并询问是否有实际例子能证明放宽约束会破坏现有代码。

• **Clone派生是基础功能，不应复杂化**：csomar认为Derive Clone是基础功能，不应复杂化，以避免意外行为，并建议将复杂情况交由第三方库处理。

补充讨论：
• **对LLM生成内容的不满**：qwertox表达了对LLM生成内容的不满，认为其解释不够准确且容易产生误导。

• **对博客内容的赞赏**：PontingClarke赞赏博客文章，认为它提醒了开发者在深层次或泛型类型中使用派生Clone时可能带来的微妙行为。xupybd则对博客作者的年龄表示惊讶。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于是否应强制所有泛型参数实现Clone，以及当前的派生机制是否需要增加复杂性以处理更多情况。一部分人认为应保持简单，另一部分则希望增加自定义选项或强制泛型参数实现Clone。

impl
Eq
) {}
fn
main
() {
let
x
=
WrapAlwaysEq
(
AlwaysEq
(NotEq));
assert_is_eq
(x);
}
The second example is a bit far fetched, but you probably answered yes.
But
neither
do
.
Why not?
The
implementation of
#[derive(Clone)] in the Rust compiler
generates a
Clone
implementation with the following requirements on the
derived type:
All fields must be
Clone
.
All generic parameters must be
Clone
.
Can you spot the issue here? It's the latter requirement:
we cannot just
require all generic parameters to be
Clone
, as we cannot assume they are used
in such a way that requires them to be cloned
.
^1
This applies to practically all builtin derive traits, such as
Clone
,
PartialEq
,
Eq
, or
even
Debug
.
What can we do to fix this?
There are two solutions to this. Both require deleting that second requirement.
The hard way
We could create a Rust RFC, hopefully not bikeshed it to death, and get it
stabilized in the next Rust edition as it is a breaking change.
^2
This would take 4+ years to stabilize and be available to everyone. That sucks,
but is the correct thing to do in the long-term.
The quick way
We can just write our own macro that generates the following code:
/* input */
#[derive(CustomClone)]
struct
WrapArc
<T>(Arc<T>);
/* generated code */
impl
<T>
Clone
for
WrapArc
<T>
where
Arc<T>:
Clone
,
// and so on, `FieldType: DerivedTrait` for each field
{
// ...
}
This does the job correctly.
And it's not even hard to do. I know people who do this internally in their
company codebases - it's not much code.
So I've
opened an issue
about replicating the builtin derive traits in a less restrictive and thus
correct way in the
derive_more
crate's GitHub repository. The reason I chose
this crate is because it already has a lot of users and is the main place for
derive implementations.
Replicating already-existing behaviour of the std may not be in the scope of the
crate, which is a perfectly fine stance to take. If that doesn't get accepted,
I'll probably create my own crate and release it on
crates.io
.
Stay tuned, I'll update this blog post.
The reason this is the way it
is is probably because Rust's type system wasn't powerful enough for this to be
implemented back in the pre-1.0 days. Or it was just a simple oversight that got
stabilized.
..?
Surely it is a
breaking change, or the compiler people would've fixed it already. Right?
..?
44467657.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了Rust中自动派生 trait（如 `Clone`、`PartialEq` 等）的当前实现问题。具体来说，派生这些 trait 时，编译器要求所有泛型参数也必须实现对应的 trait，但这并不总是合理的。文章通过两个代码示例展示了这一问题：

1. 一个包含 `Arc` 的结构体在派生 `Clone` 时出错，因为编译器默认要求泛型参数 `T` 也实现 `Clone`，但实际上不需要。
2. 另一个示例展示了类似的问题，结构体 `WrapAlwaysEq` 包含一个泛型类型 `AlwaysEq`，在进行 `PartialEq` 和 `Eq` 比较时出现问题。

文章提出了两种解决方案：
1. 长期方案是提交RFC，进行讨论和稳定化，但这可能需要数年时间。
2. 短期方案是编写自定义宏来实现更灵活的派生逻辑，作者选择在 `derive_more` crate 中提出问题，并考虑创建新 crate。

最终，作者希望改进Rust中派生 trait 的实现方式，以避免不必要的泛型限制。

data.author: hasheddan
data.article_summary:
Berry是一种超轻量、动态类型的嵌入式脚本语言，专为低性能嵌入式设备设计。其解释器核心代码小于40KiB，可在低于4KiB的堆上运行（基于ARM Cortex M4 CPU）。Berry使用单通道编译器和基于寄存器的虚拟机，所有代码均用ANSI C99编写。简单值类型（如int、boolean、string）不是类对象，而list、map和range则是类对象，以提升性能。

Berry具有轻量、快速、强大、灵活和简单的特点，支持命令式、面向对象和函数式编程。它提供垃圾回收、FFI（外部函数接口）和正则表达式等功能。控制结构包括条件语句、循环语句和跳转语句。函数支持局部变量、闭包和匿名函数。类支持单继承、方法和操作符重载。模块管理支持内置和扩展模块，并可将代码固化到闪存以减少RAM使用。

Berry语法简单直观，类似于高级语言，支持映射到C代码调用。通过示例展示了类的声明、继承和使用方法。

44472246.article_content:
Berry is a ultra-lightweight dynamically typed embedded scripting language. It is designed for lower-performance embedded devices. The Berry interpreter-core's code size is less than 40KiB and can run on less than 4KiB heap (on ARM Cortex M4 CPU, Thumb ISA and ARMCC compiler).
The interpreter of Berry include a one-pass compiler and register-based VM, all the code is written in ANSI C99. In Berry not every type is a class object. Some simple value types, such as int, real, boolean and string are not class object, but list, map and range are class object. This is a consideration about performance. Register-based VM is the same meaning as above.
Lightweight
A well-optimized interpreter with very little resources. Ideal for use in microprocessors.
Fast
Optimized one-pass bytecode compiler and register-based virtual machine.
Powerful
Supports imperative programming, object-oriented programming, functional programming.
Flexible
Berry is a dynamic type script, and it's intended for embedding in applications. It can provide good dynamic scalability for the host system.
Simple
Simple and natural syntax, support garbage collection, and easy to use FFI (foreign function interface).
RAM saving
With compile-time object construction, most of the constant objects are stored in read-only code data segments, so the RAM usage of the interpreter is very low when it starts.

nil

true
and

List: Ordered container, like
[1, 2, 3]
Map: Hash Map container, like
{ 'a': 1, 2: 3, 'map': {} }

0..5

,

,

,

,

,

,
%

&
,

,

,
^
,
<<
,
>>
Field operator:
.
Subscript operator:
[]

+
Conditional operator: condition

:
val_false
Brackets:
()
Bytes buffer support
Control Structure
Conditional statement:
if
elif
else
end
Iteration statement:
while
,
for
Jump statement:
break
,
continue
Function
Local variable and block scope
Return statement
Nested functions definition
Closure based on Upvalue
Anonymous function
Lambda expression
Class
Inheritance (only public single inheritance)
Method and Operator Overload
Constructor method
Destructive method
Module Management
Built-in module that takes almost no RAM
Extension module support: script module, bytecode file module and shared library (like *.so, *.dll) module
Ability to solidify code, classes and modules in flash to reduce RAM usage
Optional Regex support
Optional
LVGL mapping
GC (Garbage collection)
Mark-Sweep GC
Exceptional Handling
Throw any exception value using the
raise
statement
Multiple catch mode
Bytecode file support
Export function to bytecode file
Load the bytecode file and execute
Native C interface
Can be easily embedded as a library in existing code like
Tasmota
Optional
easy mapping
to call C code from Berry
Simple and intuitive syntax
The Berry language syntax is similar to that of high-level languages and will be familiar to most programmers.
var
list
= [
"Hello"
,
"World"
]
for
text
:
list
print
(
text
)
end
Map Instance
The map class is a built-in class type that is used to provide an unordered container of key-value pairs. Within the Berry interpreter, map map uses the Hash table to implement. You can use key-value pairs to construct a map container.

= {
'greets'
:

()
return

Berry
'

}

:

(

[
i

end
Object Orientation
To use a class, you must first declare it. The declaration of a class begins with the keyword class.
The member variables and methods of the class must be specified in the declaration. This is an example of class declaration:

string

.
fname

say
()

string
.
format
(
'%s say
\n
%s %s'
,
self
.
fname
,
self
.
cname
,
"i'm your father"
)
end
end
Class inheritance
Berry only supports single inheritance, that is, a class can only have one base class, and the base class uses the operator : to declare :
Here the Child class inherits from the Parent class. The subclass will inherit all the methods and properties of the Parent class, and you can override them in the subclass. This mechanism is called Overload.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对当前传染病情况及相关因素的看法

不同观点：
• **[showmexyz的观点]**：认为有人试图通过重回无疫苗时代来“让美国再次伟大”，暗示这种做法是倒退，可能会导致过去疫苗可预防疾病的再次流行。评论带有讽刺意味，反对不接种疫苗的立场。

• **[aredox的观点]**：支持数据表明当前传染病病例已经达到甚至超过2019年爆发的水平，且年仅过半。aredox指出，过去五年本应更早出现传染病激增，但由于COVID-19大流行期间的防疫措施，其他传染病传播受到抑制。现在，由于政府高层反疫苗信息的传播和COVID重复感染，人们的免疫系统可能已经受到损害，尤其是成人和婴儿。aredox引用了多个链接来支持其观点，认为这些因素共同导致了当前的健康危机。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：反疫苗信息的传播及其对公共健康的影响。aredox认为，反疫苗运动和政府高层传播的反疫苗信息是导致传染病激增的重要原因，而showmexyz则通过讽刺的方式表达对类似现象的反对。

• **论据**：aredox引用了具体的数据和社交媒体帖子（链接）来证明其观点，包括传染病病例的增加、反疫苗信息的传播以及COVID重复感染对免疫系统的潜在影响。

• **历史背景**：showmexyz的评论暗示了历史上疫苗推广之前的状况，并通过“重温无疫苗时代”来批评当前的一些政治和公共卫生政策。

• **责任归属**：aredox将当前问题的一部分责任归咎于政府高层的反疫苗信息传播，表明这不仅仅是自然发生的传染病问题，而是与政策和信息传播有直接关系。

总结：评论主要围绕当前传染病激增的现象，讨论了反疫苗信息、政府责任和COVID对免疫系统的长期影响等问题，存在明显的立场分歧。

data.title: Is it possible to play doom on an oscilloscope using only lissajous figures?
data.author: stared
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在模拟示波器上运行《毁灭战士》（1993）游戏的可能性。通常情况下，示波器仅作为显示器连接外部电脑来显示游戏，而本文提出一个更具挑战性的想法：利用李萨如曲线（Lissajous figures）原理，仅通过示波器的输入通道生成图形来玩《毁灭战士》。作者认为，虽然理论上可行，但需要外部电脑实时进行复杂的数学转换，并将信号通过数模转换器（DAC）传输到示波器。然而，这种方法计算成本高昂，实际操作难度较大。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自定义渲染器与矢量图形显示技术

不同观点：
• [phkahler] 认为，自定义的《毁灭战士》渲染器可以直接生成边缘线条。在最坏的情况下，可以为每个表面渲染不同的纯色，然后进行边缘检测或线条转换。他还指出，精灵图应该得到单独处理。此外，他认为矢量图形仍然很酷，但在实际应用中变得罕见。

• [MarkusWandel] 指出，提到的Lissajous图形实际上是对矢量显示的重新发明，而不仅仅是对Lissajous图形的简单应用。他认为这种显示可以做很多其他事情，而不仅仅是显示Lissajous图形。

• [andy99] 对Lissajous图形部分表示不解，认为Lissajous图形是X和Y波形均为正弦波的X-Y图。他质疑X和Y通道是否可以更灵活地控制，或者这是否是挑战的一部分。

• [karmakaze] 提出了一个具体项目的想法，即如果用现代的CPU/RAM替换Vectrex的旧硬件，想知道能做什么。虽然这不再是一个复古游戏机，但认为将现代技术保存在原始机壳内并保留控制器是很有趣的。

补充讨论：
• Lissajous图形的定义和应用是讨论中的一个焦点，[andy99] 和 [MarkusWandel] 对此有不同的理解和看法。
• 不同用户对矢量图形显示技术的潜在应用和实现方式有不同的设想，比如自定义渲染器和硬件改造项目。
• [karmakaze] 的硬件改造想法引发了对复古技术与现代技术结合的讨论。

44498022.article_content:
Cherenkov
Location
Washington, DC, USA
Pronouns
He/Him/His
Getting a piece of electronics to run doom (1993) is a classic project in hobby electronics, and so far people have gotten doom to run on pretty much anything, including analog oscilloscopes. However, in all cases that I have seen, the only part of the oscilloscope that is really "running" doom is the CRT display, which is hooked directly to an external computer a la 90's game consoles.
Meanwhile, people also have managed to get  analog oscilloscopes to display some pretty extraordinary and dynamic art by carefully adding together signals according to the principle of
lissajous curves
and sending those signals through the scope's regular input channels (a good example of this is
this guy
)
Which makes me wonder: is it possible to play doom on an analog oscilloscope using graphics created only using lissajous figures?
My initial thought is that it should be possible, but it would be very computationally expensive. You would still need an external digital computer, but you'd have to be constantly performing in real time some kind of complicated mathematical transformation on doom's graphics and sending the output through a DAC to the oscilloscope.

data.title: Exploring Coroutines in PHP
data.author: doekenorg
data.article_summary:
本文探讨了PHP中的协程（Coroutines）概念及其应用。协程是一种特殊的函数，可以在执行过程中暂停并交出控制权，之后可以被恢复并继续执行。与普通函数不同，协程能够保持其内部状态，即使在暂停时也不会丢失数据。PHP通过生成器（Generators）和纤程（Fibers）来支持协程。

协程有对称与非对称、无栈与有栈之分。非对称协程只能将控制权交回给调用者，而对称协程可以决定将控制权交给哪个协程。无栈协程只能在其最外层函数暂停，而有栈协程则可以在嵌套函数中暂停和恢复，更加灵活。

PHP从5.5版本开始通过生成器引入协程功能，后续版本中纤程进一步增强了协程的实现，使其能够更高效地处理异步和非阻塞代码。理解协程是进行并发编程的重要基础。

不同观点：

• donatj表示，尽管他阅读了很多关于Fibers的资料，但从未遇到一个实际用例。他认为很多例子可以用更安全的方法实现，如有序的方法调用或链式可调用对象，而不是使用Fibers。

• zackmorris分享了他对协程的历史兴趣，特别是如何用它们简化后端状态机的复杂性。他提到使用过多个PHP包来实现这一目标，但最终转向函数式编程和数据驱动开发，认为这些方法减少了状态管理的复杂性。他对现代编程语言和框架的发展方向表达了不满。

• philo23个人认为，在PHP中从未遇到需要Fibers解决的问题。他觉得Fibers更像是为其他PHP扩展/框架提供的基础设施，而不是日常开发中直接使用的工具。

• 对PHP语言发展的整体方向和其设计决策的批评，特别是在并发和状态管理方面的能力。
